newsitem.title: CANADA: Dylex eyeing buys with up to C$25 mln capex.
newsitem.headline: Dylex eyeing buys with up to C$25 mln capex.

text.p: Retailer Dylex Ltd is mulling compatible acquisitions and expanding its store base with C$20 to C$25 million of capital expenditures for fiscal 1998, said Chief Executive Elliott Wahle on Wednesday.
"We will consider acquisitions in our more strong businesses that have a solid level of operation," Wahle said after the annual meeting. Fiscal 1998 ends in early February.
Wahle did not rule out making acquisitions in 1997.
Dylex, which shed all but C$1 million in debt after emerging from creditor protection in 1995, posted capital expenditures of C$5 million for the year ended February 3.
Wahle said their stronger chains include Thriftys, with 108 jean outlets, and its women's wear group which includes banners Braemar with 63 shops and 73 Fairweather outlets.
The retailer also owns discount department chain Biway with 277 stores and 127 Tip Top Tailors shops, which sell men's clothing.

"We believe the key is to leverage the infrastructure that we've built, stick to businesses that we understand and to try to leverage the significant improvement (in stores)," Wahle said. He added that Dylex would not expand in the U.S.
Wahle also said Dylex would spend its money on opening up to seven new Thriftys and renovating 11, in addition to unveiling three updated Tip Top outets.
Biway will have up to 35 new stores built or converted to accommodate the new format which has a cleaner look, Wahle said.
Chief Finance Officer Graeme Eadie added: "We expect that capital expenditures of this size will continue for the next few years."
CIBC-Wood Gundy Securities analyst David Brodie applauded Dylex's caution.
"They're going at a measured pace; they're not betting the farm," Brodie said.

Brodie forecast a target price of C$8.75 to C$9.00 in a year considering the changes and the move by Dylex to snap up warrants and buy its common shares from its two largest shareholders, River Road (Canada) L.L.C. and Silverton INternational Fund Ltd.
Dylex shares rose 0.25 to 7.10 on the Toronto Stock Exchange in heavy mid-afternoon trading.

Wahle noted that Dylex's efforts to upgrade stores will not be felt in sales until the second half of fiscal 1998. May sales were poor but June revenues picked up a bit ahead of Father's Day on the 15th. "We are not pleased with May sales, however as I said, we are optimistic looking forward."
On a long-term basis, Wahle forecast considerable expansion for Biway after Dylex finishes fine-tuning its look and product mix.

"We do believe Biway, which is now only located in Ontairo and sprinkled through the Maritimes, has enormous expansion potential," he said. "We could at least double the store base that we have right now in across Canada expansion."
Wahle refused to provide a possible time line for the Biway roll-out.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8109 or lydia.zajc@reuters.com))
